claim: Primed convertible fluorescent proteins (pr-pcFPs) can be used to simultaneously visualize global green and photoconverted red cell populations in mouse pre-implantation embryos.
source: Here, we exploit the advantageous properties of primed convertible fluorescent proteins (pr-pcFPs) to simultaneously visualize the global green and the photoconverted red population in order to minimize tracking uncertainties over prolonged time windows.
evidence: The abstract directly states this capability as a key feature of the method.

claim: Confined primed conversion of H2B-pr-mEosFP-labeled nuclei combined with light-sheet imaging facilitates segmentation, classification, and tracking of individual nuclei from the 4-cell stage up to the blastocyst.
source: Confined primed conversion of H2B-pr-mEosFP-labeled nuclei combined with light-sheet imaging greatly facilitates segmentation, classification, and tracking of individual nuclei from the 4-cell stage up to the blastocyst.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a main finding of the study.

claim: 45% of embryos (n = 9/19) exhibit confounding rotational and spatial drift during pre-implantation development.
source: During these early steps of development, a major fraction of embryos (n = 9/19, 45% in this study) exhibit confounding rotational and spatial drift (Videos 1, 2 and 3), which often leads researchers to exclude these embryos from analysis, drastically decreasing efficiency, losing valuable data, and potentially biasing downstream results (Strnad et al., 2016; Motosugi et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data from this study showing the proportion of embryos with drift.

claim: Embryo rotation and spatial drift often lead researchers to exclude embryos from analysis, decreasing efficiency and potentially biasing results.
source: During these early steps of development, a major fraction of embryos (n = 9/19, 45% in this study) exhibit confounding rotational and spatial drift (Videos 1, 2 and 3), which often leads researchers to exclude these embryos from analysis, drastically decreasing efficiency, losing valuable data, and potentially biasing downstream results (Strnad et al., 2016; Motosugi et al., 2005).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to previous work and describes a known problem in the field.

claim: Higher frame rates increase photodamage from laser overexposure and are less applicable for highly sensitive mouse embryos.
source: Moreover, higher frame rates increase photodamage from laser overexposure and are hence less applicable for highly sensitive mouse embryos (Strnad et al., 2016; Takenaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Primed conversion uses dual-wavelength illumination with blue 488nm and far-red 730nm laser light instead of violet light.
source: Our recent report of a novel photochemical mechanism called "primed conversion" overcomes this long-standing problem by using dual-wavelength illumination with blue 488nm and far-red 730nm laser light instead (see Mohr and Pantazis, 2018) for a review).
evidence: The manuscript describes the technical specifications of primed conversion with a citation to a review.

claim: Primed conversion allows for confined photoconversion of small volumes in three dimensions (3D) by selectively intersecting two laser beams in a common focal spot.
source: Importantly, primed conversion allows for confined photoconversion of small volumes in three dimensions (3D) by selectively intersecting the two laser beams in a common focal spot, yielding axial confinement unachievable by 405 nm photoconversion (Dempsey et al., 2015; Mohr et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work demonstrating this capability.

claim: Primed conversion yields axial confinement unachievable by 405 nm photoconversion.
source: Importantly, primed conversion allows for confined photoconversion of small volumes in three dimensions (3D) by selectively intersecting the two laser beams in a common focal spot, yielding axial confinement unachievable by 405 nm photoconversion (Dempsey et al., 2015; Mohr et al., 2016).
evidence: This comparative claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Primed convertible variants of most pcFPs have been rationally engineered with improved brightness and photostability.
source: The discovery of the mechanism responsible for primed conversion enabled the rational engineering of primed convertible ("pr-") variants of most pcFPs (Mohr et al., 2017; Turkowyd et al., 2017) with improved brightness and photostability, essential properties for long-term imaging in a SPIM (Mohr et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies describing the engineering of these variants.

claim: Embryos injected with mRNA encoding for H2B-pr-mEosFP showed no visible signs of developmental impairment, similar to un-injected control embryos.
source: Embryos injected with mRNA encoding for H2B-pr-mEosFP showed no visible signs of developmental impairment, similar to un-injected control embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a and 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and reference to figure data.

claim: H2B-pr-mEos2-injected embryos showed partly divided, seemingly connected nuclei and prematurely arrested in development (n=30/30).
source: In contrast, H2B-pr-mEos2-injected embryos showed partly divided, seemingly connected nuclei and prematurely arrested in development (n=30/30) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim provides specific quantitative data from experiments with reference to figure.

claim: The inability of H2B-pr-mEos2-injected embryos to separate nuclei during cell division is likely due to a residual tendency of mEos2 to oligomerize.
source: This apparent inability to separate the nuclei during cell division is likely due to a residual tendency of mEos2 to oligomerize, as proposed previously (Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on previous literature cited.

claim: Primed convertible mEosFP (pr-mEosFP) is the optimal fluorescent protein variant for in vivo primed conversion in the mouse embryo followed by long-term imaging.
source: As a consequence, we identified primed convertible mEosFP (pr-mEosFP) as the optimal fluorescent protein variant for in vivo primed conversion in the mouse embryo followed by long-term imaging.
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparative experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Embryos subjected to photoconversion of a single cell developed normally and the red daughter cells of the initially primed converted cell were clearly distinguishable from non-converted green cells up to the blastocyst stage.
source: Embryos subjected to photoconversion of a single cell developed normally and the red daughter cells of the initially primed converted cell were clearly distinguishable from non-converted green cells up to the blastocyst stage (Figure 1b; Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations with reference to figures.

claim: Primed conversion itself did not impede the development of photoconverted embryos compared to non-converted control embryos.
source: In addition, primed conversion itself did not impede the development of photoconverted embryos compared to non-converted control embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative experimental data with reference to figure.

claim: The percentage of embryos showing spatial and rotational drift prohibitive of automated lineage tracing in experiments with 5-minute imaging time intervals (50%, n=8) was similar to those imaged with larger time intervals (45% embryos imaged every 7.5 or 15 minutes, n=11).
source: Of note, while we initially imaged our embryos with time intervals of 7.5 or 15 minutes, we found that increased sampling frequency did not recover successful lineage tracing for rotating embryos: the percentage of embryos showing spatial and rotational drift prohibitive of automated lineage tracing in our experiments with 5-minute imaging time intervals (=50%, n=8) was similar to those imaged with larger time intervals (=45% embryos imaged every 7.5 or 15 minutes, n=11).
evidence: The claim provides specific quantitative data from experiments comparing different imaging intervals.

claim: Dual nuclear labeling allows identification of weaker fluorescent red nuclei at advanced time points by their overlap with the green signal in which lower autofluorescence was detected.
source: To discern red signal from increasing background signal, we took advantage of the dual nuclear labeling that allowed us to identify weaker fluorescent red nuclei at advanced time points by their overlap with the green signal in which lower autofluorescence was detected (Figure 2a, left column).
evidence: The claim describes a technical advantage observed in the experimental data with reference to figure.

claim: Dual color information allows for cell distinction in instances otherwise rendered ambiguous through high cell density and proximity of nuclei.
source: In addition, the dual color information allowed for cell distinction in instances otherwise rendered ambiguous through high cell density and proximity of nuclei.
evidence: The claim describes an advantage of the dual labeling approach based on experimental observations.

claim: The dual labeling approach enabled distinction of nuclei that would have been identified as a single nucleus even after manual validation.
source: For instance, we were able to distinguish nuclei that would have been identified as a single nucleus even after manual validation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-c).
evidence: The claim is supported by specific examples shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The resulting high-quality 5D cropped and registered datasets were reduced to only 34±11% of the original size.
source: The resulting high-quality 5D cropped and registered datasets were reduced to only 34±11% of the original size (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim provides specific quantitative data about data size reduction with reference to figure.

claim: None of the existing state-of-the-art lineage tracing tools such as Ilastik, TrackMate and the TGMM software were designed to compensate for heavy rotational and spatial drift and are therefore incapable of calculating lineage trees from these embryos.
source: Of note, none of the existing state-of-the-art lineage tracing tools such as Ilastik, TrackMate and the TGMM software (Amat et al., 2014) were designed to compensate for heavy rotational and spatial drift and are therefore incapable of calculating lineage trees from these embryos (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on testing existing tools and is supported by reference to source data.

claim: Separating the green and red channels to generate two less complex datasets during lineage reconstruction increased the fidelity of lineage tracing versus a dataset consisting of the green channel alone.
source: Separating the green and red channels to generate two less complex datasets during lineage reconstruction further increased the fidelity of lineage tracing versus a dataset consisting of the green channel alone (Figure 2a, right column; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The resulting lineage trees required a minimal amount of time for manual corrections (0.5-1.5 hours per lineage tree).
source: We were able to recover all rotating embryos that we acquired using this image analysis pipeline and the resulting lineage trees required a minimal amount of time for manual corrections (0.5-1.5 hours per lineage tree).
evidence: The claim provides specific quantitative data about the time required for manual corrections.

claim: Using primed Track to correct for spatial and rotational drift results in reliable reconstruction of the lineage trees even at imaging time intervals of 30 minutes for a rotating embryo and 40 minutes for a non-rotating embryo.
source: Using primed Track to correct for spatial and rotational drift results in reliable reconstruction of the lineage trees even at imaging time intervals of 30 minutes for a rotating embryo and 40 minutes for a non-rotating embryo (Figure 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing lineage tracing at different time intervals with reference to figures.

claim: The registration of non-drifting embryos does not increase lineage tracing accuracy for high 5-minute sampling rates.
source: While the registration of non-drifting embryos does not increase lineage tracing accuracy for high 5-minute sampling rates, the gain of fidelity in lineage tree reconstruction of these embryos greatly benefits from our presented approach when the imaging frequency is reduced (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is based on comparative analysis of lineage tracing accuracy at different sampling rates with reference to figure.

claim: Sampling rates above 40 minutes will decrease the possibility to precisely infer cell divisions and assign daughter cells to their correct mother.
source: However, in general, one should keep in mind that sampling rates above 40 minutes will decrease the possibility to precisely infer cell divisions and assign daughter cells to their correct mother.
evidence: This is a cautionary statement based on the limitations observed in the experimental data.

claim: Primed Track enables fast, automated, high fidelity lineage tracing of mammalian pre-implantation development combined with reduced illumination time and data volume.
source: In summary, primed Track enables fast, automated, high fidelity lineage tracing of mammalian pre-implantation development combined with reduced illumination time and data volume, key considerations for handling and analyzing data by the biological community (Pantazis and Supatto, 2014).
evidence: This summary claim is supported by the experimental results presented throughout the manuscript and a citation.

claim: The ability to correct for both spatial and rotational drift overcomes the previous requirement to exclude spinning embryos from the analysis using primed Track.
source: The ability to correct for both spatial and rotational drift overcomes the previous requirement to exclude spinning embryos from the analysis using primed Track.
evidence: This claim summarizes a key advantage of the method based on the experimental results.

claim: Primed conversion of photoconvertible proteins in combination with primed Track enables the experimenter to still achieve reasonable lineage tracing quality with datasets acquired at lower sampling rate.
source: Furthermore, primed conversion of photoconvertible proteins in combination with primed Track enables the experimenter to still achieve reasonable lineage tracing quality with datasets acquired at lower sampling rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing successful lineage tracing at reduced sampling rates.

claim: Low abundant protein fusions may require higher illumination power for visualization, potentially impacting sample integrity.
source: While we present tracking and lineage tracing of embryos labeled with a relatively highly-expressed and stable H2B-pr-pcFP fusion protein, it is important to take into consideration that low abundant protein fusions may require higher illumination power for visualization, potentially impacting sample integrity.
evidence: This is a cautionary statement based on general knowledge about fluorescence imaging.

source: C57Bl/6 wild-type females (Janvier Labs, France) were superovulated by hormone priming, mated to C57Bl/6 males (RRID:IMSR_JAX:000664), and mated females were euthanized by CO2 asphyxiation.

source: mRNA constructs were microinjected into the pro-nucleus at 50 ng/µl or in both cells in two-cell stage embryos, following standard protocols.

claim: Green and red labels can be used as fiducial markers to computationally correct for rotational and translational drift.
source: Using green and red labels as fiducial markers, we computationally correct for rotational and translational drift, reduce overall data size, and accomplish high-fidelity lineage tracing even for increased imaging time intervals – addressing major concerns in the field of volumetric embryo imaging.

claim: The primed Track approach reduces overall data size.
source: Using green and red labels as fiducial markers, we computationally correct for rotational and translational drift, reduce overall data size, and accomplish high-fidelity lineage tracing even for increased imaging time intervals – addressing major concerns in the field of volumetric embryo imaging.

claim: Primed Track accomplishes high-fidelity lineage tracing even for increased imaging time intervals.
source: Using green and red labels as fiducial markers, we computationally correct for rotational and translational drift, reduce overall data size, and accomplish high-fidelity lineage tracing even for increased imaging time intervals – addressing major concerns in the field of volumetric embryo imaging.

claim: Accurate lineage reconstruction of mammalian pre-implantation development is essential for inferring the earliest cell fate decisions.
source: Accurate lineage reconstruction of mammalian pre-implantation development is essential for inferring the earliest cell fate decisions.

source: However, to our knowledge these sparse labels have not been combined with SPIM - presumably because photoconversion has been limited by the need for axially unconfined, potentially photodamaging, intense violet light (Post et al., 2005).

source: Labeling strategies using green-to-red photoconvertible fluorescent proteins (pcFPs) allow for visualization of both the entire population of cells in green and a selected population in red.

source: This combination of global and sparse labeling yields great potential for facilitating lineage tracing and trophectoderm (TE) and inner-cell-mass (ICM) fate assignments after photoconversion (Kurotaki et al., 2007).

source: Here, we show that primed conversion of single pr-pcFP-labeled cells in early stages of mouse development allows for computational correction of spatial and rotational drift, which minimizes uncertainties in tracking and lineage tracing.

claim: Primed conversion of single pr-pcFP-labeled cells minimizes uncertainties in tracking and lineage tracing.
source: Here, we show that primed conversion of single pr-pcFP-labeled cells in early stages of mouse development allows for computational correction of spatial and rotational drift, which minimizes uncertainties in tracking and lineage tracing.

N ≥ 200 embryos out of ≥10 independent experiments. Scale bar, 20 µm.

claim: The automatic tracking of a realigned embryo resulted in greatly improved lineage tracing fidelity compared to a naïve state-of-the-art lineage-tracing algorithm that was not able to reconstruct a lineage tree from rotating and spatially drifting embryos imaged with a time interval of 15, 7.5 or 5 minutes.
source: The automatic tracking of a realigned embryo resulted in greatly improved lineage tracing fidelity compared to a naïve state-of-the-art lineage-tracing algorithm that was not able to reconstruct a lineage tree from rotating and spatially drifting embryos imaged with a time interval of 15, 7.5 or 5 minutes (Bitplane Imaris cell lineage package) (Figure 2b; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: The Bitplane Imaris cell lineage package was not able to reconstruct a lineage tree from rotating and spatially drifting embryos imaged with a time interval of 15, 7.5 or 5 minutes.
source: The automatic tracking of a realigned embryo resulted in greatly improved lineage tracing fidelity compared to a naïve state-of-the-art lineage-tracing algorithm that was not able to reconstruct a lineage tree from rotating and spatially drifting embryos imaged with a time interval of 15, 7.5 or 5 minutes (Bitplane Imaris cell lineage package) (Figure 2b; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
